realPrompts.note: D4 A: P3 orbit-bash as SHELL; HOME, profile and variable names agent commands see

checks.name: a token is exchanged from the key without a prompt (file store, session/new)
session/new succeeds with both CURSOR_API_KEY and CURSOR_AUTH_TOKEN set
the CLI starts orbit-bash (a #!/bin/sh script whose path names bash) for the agent's commands
…for the login-shell snapshot (-ilc) as well as for each command (-c)
detail: # Or execute directly (captures a subshell's state):
# Require base64 for safe encoding of emitted sections
# Helper to log timing, only if DUMP_BASH_STATE_TIMING is set
# Helper to append a line to output file
# Helper to safely encode and emit unsafe values
# Builtin printf, not a here-document: no argument length limit, and no temp file
# Emit start marker at the very beginning of the output
# Drop ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE by exact name so one command exporting it can't
# bake it into the snapshot that every later command re-evals (IDE-2911:
# Cypress boots as plain Node until a new chat). Exact unset rather than the
# line-based grep below, which would also eat vars whose name or multiline
# value merely contains the token. The shell exits right after the dump.
# Filter out: proxy settings plus request/session-scoped vars that must not
# POSIX shell options (replayable as set +/-o lines). Exclude the errexit/nounset/
# pipefail this function force-enables above, so they are not baked into the restored
# snapshot and leaked onto every subsequent command (a stray pipefail makes a
# Bash shopt options (replayable as shopt -s/-u lines)

-O extglob -c IFS= builtin read -r -d '' __cursor_command <&5 2>/dev/null || { builtin printf '%s\n' 'The command did not run: a shell startup file ($BASH_ENV or .zshenv) closed or replaced file descriptor 5, which carries the command. Run it again; this shell now passes commands as arguments.' >&2; builtin exit 126; }; exec 5<&-; builtin set -- "$__cursor_command"; builtin unset __cursor_command; snap=$(command cat <&3) && builtin shopt -s extglob && builtin eval -- "$snap" && { builtin set +u 2>/dev/null || true; builtin eval "${__CURSOR_SANDBOX_ENV_RESTORE:-}" 2>/dev/null; builtin eval "${__CURSOR_SANDBOX_TEMP_RESTORE:-}" 2>/dev/null; builtin export PWD="$(builtin pwd)"; builtin shopt -s expand_aliases 2>/dev/null; builtin eval "$1" < /dev/null; }; COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=$?; dump_bash_state >&4; builtin exit $COMMAND_EXIT_CODE --

checks.name: agent commands see the runner user's HOME (the wrapper's), not the CLI's account HOME
…and its login profile, not the account HOME's
…and none of CURSOR_API_KEY, CURSOR_AUTH_TOKEN, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR, CURSOR_DATA_DIR
a workspace variable still reaches them (the canary)
the CLI itself still runs on the account HOME: its state file is there, nothing of Cursor's in the commands' HOME
the runner user's real ~/.cursor, ~/.config/cursor and ~/.local/share/cursor-agent are untouched
